title: Bayes’ theorem as a probability identity
dek: P(A | B) = P(B | A) P(A) / P(B). That is a swap of conditioning, after you rebuild P(B). Parameter posteriors are the same identity with a prior on θ — a different plate.
story: Once P(B) > 0, Bayes’ theorem is the definition of conditional probability with the intersection expanded the other way: P(A | B) = P(B | A) P(A) / P(B). You have not introduced a prior-as-belief until you choose to read A as a parameter. You have swapped which event is the slice, and you owe the reader a marginal for B.

The denominator is the law of total probability. If {A, Aᶜ} partitions, P(B) = P(B | A) P(A) + P(B | Aᶜ) P(Aᶜ). Diagnostic PPV is this arithmetic with A = disease and B = test positive. Sensitivity P(B | A) is not P(A | B). Skipping P(A) is how a 99% sensitive assay is quoted as a 99% chance of TB.

The same algebra with A = “θ in a set” and B = “data in a set” becomes a posterior probability. The inference plate (stats-bayesian) is that culture: a prior density, a likelihood function, MCMC when the marginal is ugly. This plate stays on events you can name without a sampler — a smear, an Ultra call, a lineage tag — and on the odds form that makes the swap hard to fudge.
deepTitle: Odds form, two kinds of A, and what the identity refuses
deep: Odds form: posterior odds = likelihood ratio × prior odds. For a binary A, P(A | B)/P(Aᶜ | B) = [P(B | A)/P(B | Aᶜ)] × [P(A)/P(Aᶜ)]. The likelihood ratio is a property of the test given the two worlds; prevalence sits only in the prior odds.

Two different A’s. Event A: disease, RR-TB, “this isolate is mixed.” Parameter A: π in (0.1, 0.2), a regression coefficient. Same identity, different σ-algebra. The glossary card wiki-bayes-theorem is the shared slogan; stats-predictive-values is the diagnostic PPV/NPV worksheet; stats-bayesian is θ as a random variable.
P(B) = 0 makes the ratio undefined. Continuous data need densities; do not divide by P(exactly this 24-digit MIC vector).
A likelihood ratio for a diagnostic test is not Wilks’ Λ for nested models, and it is not a Bayes factor (ratio of marginal likelihoods). Those own plates exist because the words collide.
Independence of A and B would make P(A | B) = P(A): the likelihood ratio is 1 and the theorem is a no-op. Household clustering is the usual reason that “independence” was a wish.

formulas.label: Probability form
formulas.expression: P(A | B) = P(B | A) P(A) / P(B)    (P(B) > 0)
formulas.note: Rebuild P(B) with a partition. Sensitivity is P(B | A), not this left-hand side.

formulas.label: Odds form (binary A)
formulas.note: LR(B) = P(B | A)/P(B | Aᶜ). Prevalence enters only through prior odds O(A).

visual.caption: Bayes as a swap: start from P(B | A) and a prior P(A), rebuild the marginal P(B) from both worlds, then invert to P(A | B). Diagnostic A and parameter θ are the same arrows with different labels — they are not the same scientific object.

example.title: RR-TB prior 3%, assay LR+ = 20
example.setup: Community prevalence of rifampin-resistant TB among people tested is P(R) = 0.03. A rapid rpoB assay has P(+ | R) = 0.90 and P(+ | Rᶜ) = 0.045, so LR+ = 0.90/0.045 = 20. Someone says “90% sensitive, so 90% chance this person is RR.”

steps.title: The same number from the probability form
Change the prior, keep the assay
steps.body: In a DR-TB ward with P(R) = 0.40, posterior odds = 20 × 0.40/0.60 ≈ 13.3, so P(R | +) ≈ 0.93. The likelihood ratio did not change. The event R did.

example.takeaway: Bayes swaps conditioning after you rebuild P(B). Prevalence is that rebuild, not an optional mood.

check.prompt: P(A | B) equals P(B | A) when:
choices: Always; that is what “inverse probability” means
Only in special cases (for example P(A) = P(B)); in general you must multiply by P(A)/P(B)
Whenever A is a disease and B is a test
check.answer: Only in special cases (for example P(A) = P(B)); in general you must multiply by P(A)/P(B)
check.why: The theorem is a reweighting by the two priors, not a free swap of labels.

whyWrong.Always; that is what “inverse probabilit: That is the classic error the identity exists to stop.
whyWrong.Whenever A is a disease and B is a test: Diagnostic use is the setting where the swap error is most expensive, not where it becomes legal.
whyWrong.Whenever you have used MCMC: MCMC is how you compute a parameter posterior, not a licence to equate P(A|B) with P(B|A).

whyWrong.0.99: That is sensitivity P(B|A), not the posterior.

check.prompt: On the flow map, two end nodes after P(A | B) exist because:
choices: The identity only applies to diseases
A might be a named event (disease, RR-TB) or a parameter; Simplfy splits those into different plates
You must run MCMC before quoting P(A | B) for a test
Prior odds are illegal in diagnosis
check.answer: A might be a named event (disease, RR-TB) or a parameter; Simplfy splits those into different plates
check.why: Same arrows, different objects. Diagnostic PPV versus a posterior on θ.

whyWrong.The identity only applies to diseases: It applies to any events with P(B) > 0, including parameters once you put a prior on them.
whyWrong.You must run MCMC before quoting P(A | B: Binary diagnosis is finite arithmetic; MCMC is for ugly integrals.
whyWrong.Prior odds are illegal in diagnosis: Prevalence is the prior odds. Hiding it is the error.
